english: [TAB]Thus spoke the Martyr Mishahel, as the Luonnotar stood chained in the city plaza awaiting Junil's justice: [PARAGRAPH:1]"You ask us to repent? We ask you the same. We are all Children of The One, you, and I, and all your so-called gods alike, no matter who denies it. His angels may have made this world, but only by His leave. This warrants them no worship. We will adore only The One. The Twenty-One have all sinned and fallen short of the glory of The One, by far more than the vilest mortal falls short of your Junil's majesty. Our Elder Brothers, the angels, swore to guide us to enlightenment, to make us all their equals. Instead, like petulant children, they have turned their charges into pawns for petty squabbles among themselves. Now it falls to us to enlighten them. Fighting evil with evil can never be called justice. Junil is no better than Agares, only a greater hypocrite. Every "god" willing joined Agares' rebellion. They are all oath-breakers. The All-Father offered his children true freedom, but from fear and lust for power they have chosen bondage. Agares stole the Gems of Creation and forged their links to the infinite planes, but each "god" gladly enslaved his own soul to his to a separate precept. Our own sire, Nemed, came near to redemption when he surrendered his divinity, but in his folly defied The One and damned us all to "immortality. " Only The One should last forever. I endure only by his will. This world soon shall pass away. We will all be judged. Perhaps some shall escape Creation and enter into the True Heaven. Repent now while there is still a chance, lest you instead be punished along with your idols. "[PARAGRAPH:2]With this their trial was over. The Priors had heard enough. Such egregious blasphemy demanded special punishment. Hanging or decapitation would not suffice. These fools must be made an example to the public in the most dramatic way: a Pillar of Fire called down from the heavens. The Pontiff's prayers had been answered with the miracle on multiple occasions during the late war against The Ashen Veil, and he knew Junil would be eager to purge this greater scourge. [PARAGRAPH:2]Junil indeed hated the gospel of the Luonnotar, because he feared it might be true. How could any mortal know such things? The terms of The Compact forbid any angel from sharing such secrets with the living. One worry filled his soul with terror: could The One have returned, and revealed himself only to these mortals? Impossible. . . or was it? Junil was now forced to doubt his own righteousness. Was not Agares first great sin the creation of a world and people required to worship him, and kept in ignorance of the truth? This line of thought would have gone on, until he recalled an obscure clause that Dagda's Archangel had inserted into The Compact which precisely dictated his proper course action. He suppressed his existential angst by following the letter of the law as usual. [PARAGRAPH:2]The people watched in awe as they saw the flames descending from the sky, with greater force than had ever descended before. The Prior was certain of his victory, while the Luonnotar stoically accepted their unjust fate. No one predicted what came next. The pillar descended and engulfed them, but not a hair on their heads or a fiber of their clothing was singed. The same could not be said of the chains binding them, or the flesh of their persecutors, or the stones of the Basilica itself, which rapidly melted away. Half the city cried in anguish, and were reduced to ash. The only survivors within miles of the plaza were the condemned, and those who had hearkened to their words. [PARAGRAPH]Rumors spread that the basilica was burned by sorcery, and armies amassed to avenge the massacre. Assailed at every stop, the Luonnotar always proved invulnerable to divine magic yet often fell to mundane blades. They continued to preach and attract new converts, but were always on the verge of extinction until finding sanctuary among the Grigori. Cassiel sent word assuring them that they could live in peace within his realm so long as they never tried to emulate their persecutors. Refugees of all faiths were welcome to live in peace among the Grigori, if they could tolerate that blasphemy was the national pastime. The Luonnotar gained a base from which to organize evangelism abroad, but rarely won converts among their skeptical new compatriots. Mishahel continued to petition the fallen archangel for an audience and for some endorsement for his beliefs, but was always ignored. The one blasphemy Cassiel cannot tolerate is the notion that The One is petty enough to desire any cult of worshipers. [PARAGRAPH:3]The Children of The One religion may start in either one two ways: through a random event that may occur in any city under any state religion, or the Grigori civilization discovering [LINK=TECH_ARCANE_LORE]Arcane Lore[\\LINK]. [PARAGRAPH]Cities with this and another faith are both present have a chance of triggering a Monotheist Revolt, in which this faith will force its competitors out. If the religion removed was a state religion, then the city will revolt as if newly conquered. The Children of The One itself can never be a state religion. [PARAGRAPH]The [LINK=UNIT_LUONNOTAR]Luonnotar[\\LINK], the religion's only unique unit, can travel through rival territory without open boarder agreements in order to spread its faith among cities and units alike. Priests of other religions who adopt this faith are defrocked--the units are automatically deleted if anyone tries to use them. The Luonnotar unit is immune to magic and has no spells of its own, but is very strong against disciple units and will target them even in stacks with better defenders. Any unit which converts to this religion becomes [LINK=PROMOTION_MAGIC_RESISTANCE]resistant to magic[\\LINK] and also [LINK=PROMOTION_REBEL]rebellious[\\LINK] against any owner that is running any state religion. If a leader with a state religion orders such units to fight against the Grigori, they will most likely defect. The religion's only building is its holy shrine, [LINK=BUILDING_UNHARMED_MARTYRS]The Unmarred Martyrs[\\LINK]. This provides [LINK=BONUS_MANA_FORCE]Force mana[\\LINK], great person points towards [LINK=UNIT_ADVENTURER]Adventurers[\\LINK], and increased war weariness for your enemies. Units in the city are 100% resistant to magic, gain the Scourge promotion, and lose the [LINK=PROMOTION_DIVINE]Divine[\\LINK] promotion (priests loose access to their spells just by passing through the city). It makes other religious buildings cause a great deal of unhappiness. [PARAGRAPH]Units of this religion will never return as either [LINK=UNIT_ANGEL]Angels[\\LINK] or [LINK=UNIT_MANES]Manes[\\LINK]. \r\n[PARAGRAPH:3]All priests have their Ardas weakened by the presence of the Children of the One, especially in cities nearby.  Once the Children of the One have enough influence, priests may abandon their faith and become rebellious, possibly disbanding themselves of defecting to the Grigori.

[TAB]There have been men have worshiped The White Hand of Mulcarn in every era since before the time of the Godswar, but they have never been many. During the Age of Magic, his stoic Frost Speakers were tolerated but disrespected. Mulcarn was considered the least of the gods, at a time when his nemesis Bhall was considered the greatest. Although the least evil of all those who sided with Agares against The One, he was a supremely jealous god who grew to greatly hate humanity for their devotion to every god but himself. As Nostalgia is his very nature, he longed to return to how things were in the Godswar, when man was a primitive being subject to the whims of the divine and gods were not bound by the regulations of The Compact. [TAB]The Fall of Bhall gave him an opportunity to make this a reality. With no god to oppose him, he was able to maneuver the one people who honored him, the nearly destitute Illians, into completing a ritual that summoned him into the plane of Erebus. Sucellus was sent to enforce The Compact and prevent Mulcarn's conquest of the world, but he failed in his endeavor. His body was broken in seven pieces and buried in distant regions of the infinite plane, to prevent them from being reunited and allowing his spirit to return from the Netherworld to challenge The God of Winter again. Where a god failed, and man succeeded. Kylorin, Archmage of the Seventh Circle and former Emperor of All Mankind, was sent on a mission by Nantosuelta (the Goddess of Enchantment and Virtue, who loved Sucellus greatly) to end The Age of Ice and retrieve the Heart of Sucellus from within Mulcarn's citadel. (She had already managed to have the other six pieces of his body gathered together. ) He gathered and reforged the pieces of the Godslayer, a weapon created as a symbol and manifestation of The Compact, and destroyed Mulcarn once and for all. [PARAGRAPH]With their god vanquished, the followers of The Hand fell to an all time low. They were slow to adapt to a changing world, and reviled by more powerful nations who had been their subjects. The few who maintained the faith however were more fanatical than ever. They realized that the true object of worship was not the person of the god, but his precept. His precept remains, and possessed a powerful will to regain an avatar. It has chosen Auric Ulvin, an orphan from a small outlying Illian village called Brigdarrow, to lead it. He is the greatest magical prodigy born in the current age, and was a very good natured child before the precept claimed him. Driven mad with power, he may end up more evil than Mulcarn ever was by the time he completes his goal and ascends into godhood. [PARAGRAPH:1]This state religion is a prerequisite of [LINK=PROJECT_THE_DEEPENING]The Deepening[\LINK], [LINK=PROJECT_THE_DRAW]The Draw[\LINK], and the [LINK=PROJECT_ASCENSION]Ascension[\LINK] rituals.

[TAB]Forgotten and ignored by the gods, some mortals have turned to worshiping the great dragons who once fought over the land and now lie dormant beneath it. They do not form any unified faith, but are a collection of many conflicting minor cults devoted to different beasts. All agree that the gods' weapons of mass destruction are themselves divine, and find their draconic deities to be much more acceptable than empty prayers offered in temples. All seek to awaken these weapons of mass destruction and see them wreak havoc on their enemies. [PARAGRAPH]These cults can pop up in any land, but are most accepted among the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_KURIOTATES]Kuriotates[\\LINK] and [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SHEAIM]Sheaim[\\LINK]. Those civilizations can complete the [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\\LINK] ritual in any city, spreading the Cult to that city, rather than only completing it in a city where the faith is already present. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Cult of the Dragon is unlike other religions. It is not founded by being the first to research a technology. It typically begins when the barbarians create [LINK=UNIT_ACHERON]Acheron's [\\LINK] [LINK=BUILDING_WYRMHOLD]Wyrmhold[\\LINK] in one of their cities and calls the great Furnace Dragon into the world. It can also be founded by the Kuriotates world spell [LINK=SPELL_LEGENDS]Legends[\\LINK], which moves the holy city to the site where it was cast and spreads the religion and the caster's culture to random cities, or by the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_KURIOTATES]Kuriotates[\\LINK] or [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SHEAIM]Sheaim[\\LINK]completing [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\\LINK].[PARAGRAPH]The Dragon Cult has numerous disadvantages for most civilizations, although these do not apply to the Kuriotates, the Sheaim, or anyone whose team controls a Dragon. It makes an empire harder to manage and control. Cities that are home to a Dragon Cult are likely to revolt. Anyone with the Fanaticism technology can train a [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_FANATIC]Dragon Fanatic[\\LINK] in a Cult city and use it to spread negative effects to rival cities. These Fanatics can be transformed into devotees of specific dragons when they visit their Wyrmholds or hear them [LINK=SPELL_ROAR]Roar[\\LINK]. A standard Fanatic will follow any dragon, but once devoted to a specific beast it will ignore the calls of other dragon species. Dragons generated by Wyrmholds start as sedentary lair guardians, but a Fanatic can use the [LINK=SPELL_BESEECH_DRAGON]Beseech Dragon[\\LINK] ability to call the beasts forth from their lairs and try to convince them to attack their enemies. There is a chance that a Dragon will spawn under your control, if you have the right mana, alignment, and follow the Cult of the Dragon as your State Religion. You cannot adopt this as your State religion unless you already have a Dragon.

[TAB]the Laeran Cord thrived throughout the Age of Magic, when the knowledge they curated was prized. These priests of Oghma were welcome in most realms, for they shared their lore freely with all who yearned to learn and stayed as neutral as the god they served. [PARAGRAPH:1]The Age of Ice spelled their ruin. Oghma ignored their prayers to save them. Embarr might have helped, but Ceridwen slayed and tore the archangel asunder, scattering his mind, flesh, and spirit across creation. [PARAGRAPH:1]All original research ceased as the order desperately labored to protect what humanity would need to know to rebuild civilization. The mages among in their ranks were not enough to save them as they fled back to ever fewer hidden libraries. The savage Doviello delighted in their demise, burning both books and men whenever found. [PARAGRAPH:1]In time their hunting parties stopped returning. Some priests went mad. Others died of starvation, or old age. the Laeran Cord dwindled to a single man: a scholar with nothing but a frozen world to study, a teacher without anyone to teach, a high priest only by default. His true name is forgotten. We know him now simply as "Akharien," which means "the last one" in the ancient tongue. [PARAGRAPH:1]In time, the Doviello came for him. Still a young man, born well into the Age of Ice, he knew nothing of world outside what he read in the last library's books. They offered a chance to flee, to survive as a wolf in the wilderness, to one day win the right to join the pack and hunt with them. [PARAGRAPH:1]Instead he threw himself on the books. He begged them to burn him but only spare the library. He promised to tell them all the stories contained within, and to teach them all about the medicinal uses of the few herb that survived in the region. [PARAGRAPH:1]They rejected his offer, believing as they did that the strong need no such knowledge and that the weak it helps preserve deserve to die. This last priest of the Laeran Cord was burned to death within his library. [PARAGRAPH:1]His spirit never passed to Oghma's vault. It lingered to haunt the ruins, fluttering among the dust and ashes which once were books. His ghost had more power than he ever did in life. It scared the Doviello away, but blessed other Vagrants with dreams of distant times and places to inspire them. [PARAGRAPH:1]A new Laeran Cord was refounded early in the Age of Rebirth. The new priests discovered the meager ruins of The Last One's library, but nothing of value remained within except the High Priest's Crown. This was taken to the new church that it might serve Oghma again. It is rumored that the spirit of Akharien followed, and continues to guide the order in relearning what was forgotten. [PARAGRAPH]There is a heresy that emerged within the Cord, rejecting the benevolent guidance of Akharien and wishing to risk experiments with darker forms of magic. Gaelan was a talented summoner and mage in the Laeran Cord. Frustrated with the slow progress within the Cord, Gaelan started the Circle of Gaelan. The Circle gained a reputation for dangerous acts followed by tragedy. While they still believed they were serving Oghma, the new faith in fact followed Ceridwen. There were escaped summoned creatures, death of livestock, a fire that nearly destroyed a village and human experimentation. The worst mistake of the Circle of Gaelan was an attempt to summon a True Angel of Prophecy. They managed to summon A Root of Fear, an Aspect of Mammon whose power had been changed from true Foresight to Foreboding of horrors that become self-fulfilling prophecies. Their greatest fear came true, and the confinement circle failed. The Root of Fear killed all the members except Gaelan himself, drowning them in fears until there was nothing left of them. The vision destroyed Gaelan's body and mind. His past was forgotten, his body horribly disfigured. The battle spread to Euphoria, the Dreamworld where Gaelan's Mind Palace was shattered by Caer lest it fall to Fear. This spread nightmares across Creation. Gaelan himself was reborn as a priest of the Undertow, known only as the Burnt Priest. As the faith of the Matronae spreads, and other religions loose influence on the world, the ability of the old gods to act in Erebus wanes. If the Matronae faith reaches 100% of the world population, divine magic will die and all priests will be useless. [PARAGRAPH:2]History:[PARAGRAPH]At the end of the Age of Rebirth the demon plagued lands of the Fane of Lessers were conquered and the Throne of Hell destroyed. Not content to just cleanse creation, the archangel Basium lead his angelic army into hell to continue his war. Decades passed and in that time the Bannor used the Crucible to weaken the world's magic. Powerful artifacts of past ages became dusty relics, and those with the talent to be mages in prior ages were rarely able to manifest their power. The Age of Invention had started. [PARAGRAPH]During this age three new goddesses appeared on creation, they were known as the Matronae. Morrigan was the goddess of fate and a great white temple was built to her on the cliffs of the Elohim city of Niveus. From Niveus came the gas Effluvium, which powered city lamp posts and caused divine visions (and would also be used by the Kuriotates to build airships). Sarabride was the goddess of vengeance and her temple was a great foundry built in the reclaimed city of Braduk the Burning. From her city came all sorts of wonders including coal powered trains. The citizens of Braduk built rail systems to connect the major cities of men. The last was Cliodna, the goddess of dreams, and her temple was built on the docks of the Bay of Laurus. From her temple came great steam powered ships that opened up travel to the distant shores of creation. [PARAGRAPH]All three goddesses were active in creation and their religions grew quickly. The religions of ages past, of distant gods who might answer occasional prayers were forgotten, or destroyed by the followers of the Matronae. What use is myth when gods walk among us?[PARAGRAPH:2]The Matronae are the guises assumed by the archangels Gyra, Condatis, and Brigit, who acquired three Masks of the Coven of the Black Candle and used them to steal three Gems of Creation from their respective gods' vaults. They are not interested in becoming gods, or receiving worship. They cannot become avatars that embody their dominions. The compact does not bind them, so they don't need worshipers to permit their actions in any region. They cannot have priests with divine powers, since they don't control a dominion, don't have a fleet of angels to bless their followers, etc. But they are all archangels of fallen gods and they are worried about their dominions becoming corrupted. There is little they can do about it directly, though wars are beginning to start over it. Arak and the Gossamer Legion are coming for Morrigan. After the attack on hell, madness begins spreading through Lanun and Elohim lands as Hastur moves against Cliodna. And the battle between the Swanmay and Sarabride is a prelude to waking up Bhall. [PARAGRAPH]The goal of the Matronae is a lesson from Cassiel. They want to kill worship of the old gods so that the compact keeps them from being able to act in creation. But where Cassiel preached about how the old gods were unworthy, the Matronae have replaced those religions with new fake ones. If they can wipe out the old religions, the gods won't be able to impact creation and damage done by corrupted dominions will be mitigated. They are also reducing the ability of all the gods by claiming the gems. The gods no longer have infinite wells to draw from in three of the six materials. This doesn't mean they aren't powerful, but if the Godswar restarted the gods would be much weaker without the gems. [PARAGRAPH]The Matronae are working closely together. Sarabride and Cliodna are not opposed despite the fact that they are archangels from opposed dominions. They certainly don't agree on everything, but they are working toward the same plan. They rescued Basium from Hell with the hope that he could recover the Font of Life (and Gyra makes a habit of rescuing her idealistic brother), though Basium is nearly destroyed and the Font is guarded by an active god, and they don't currently have another mask (which wouldn't be absolutely necessary, but would certainly help). [PARAGRAPH:2]The Matronae wear Masks of the Coven of the Black Candle for a number of reasons. Protecting their identity is a big one, though in time powers will assume or know who they are. The more they can minimize this the better. Powerful sorcerers can summon and bind archangels (although the Crucible makes this difficult, if not impossible), so the Matronae do not want anyone knowing who they are. They also want to diminish any belief in the old religions, not support it by having people know they are a part of it. Most importantly the masks prevent detection. Anyone hunting, scrying, summoning them won't be able to find them with the masks on. In time, however, the truth will come out. [PARAGRAPH]It is not common knowledge that the Opalus Mortis, Corundum Ardens, and Beryllus Abyssi have been stolen in the first place. Other gods (much less mortals) cannot see into the vaults where Arawn, Bhall, and Danalin once kept them. The gods only knew that a new religion had started centered around some very powerful figures. The evil gods could however deduce the source of their powers and guess at their identities from what happened during their attack on hell. Arak (who has been fighting Gyra for centuries since she killed his wife) and Laroth are also onto Morrigan. [PARAGRAPH:3]All priests have their Ardas weakened by the presence of the Matronae in the world, especially in cities nearby. Once the Matronae influence is strong enough, priests in the vicinity of Apostates will abdondon their leaders and become Apostates themselves

Aristocrats in many lands say "Noblesse oblige. " They believe they must at least appear virtuous, in order to inspire hope and loyalty among the commoners. The Calabim deride such delusions. The Grand Broods know that the victims of the worst abuse are often the most loyal. With methods both magic and mundane, the Brood Guards turn broken souls into fanatics. Calabim thralls fear nothing more than their masters, and would more gladly slit their own throats or wrestle a dragon than risk a Vampire's slightest displeasure. Some learn to enjoy submission. Many tolerate it for the chances it offers to dominate others. A few cling to ambitions of rising in the ranks, perhaps even to becoming a Vampire Lord. Some believe that existence is nothing but suffering, that the heavens are no better than the hells, and that the only escape for an immortal soul is the nirvana of a vampire's kiss. Others believe there is no such thing as a spirit, but that a consciousness can endure indefinitely if it is consumed by and merges with the mind of a Vampire. Most have toyed with several excuses in the past but have ceased trying to rationalize their attachment to the status quo. After a lifetime learning helplessness, they lack the strength of will necessary to imagine things getting better, even if they also cannot fathom them being any worse. The Broods do not care what tales the human cattle tell themselves, so long as they follow orders without question and are quick to present themselves as snacks.

[TAB]Baptism is common to many religions but the Undertow's Cultists hold the victim underwater past immersion, through the struggle, and until the floating body has become filled and heavy with the sacred waters. Then they let go and the corpse rises as the undead Drown.[PARAGRAPH:1]This ability upgrades a Warrior into the Drown. [TAB]The Undertow priestess stood quietly on the seashore, her long flowing robe dancing in the storm. She could have done this anywhere on land, but nowhere did it feel as real and invigorating as by the sea, by the storm.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Oh mighty masters, hear my call", she spread out her arms and raised her eyes upwards, towards the storm rising above the sea. "My body and mind are yours to command, my sanity but a tool at your bidding. Honor my sacrifice to you, and grant me the sight of your servant." Intoning the words, she could feel the might that lurked deep below the waves, the ancient and inhuman power. The overwhelming sensation was enough to blind her to the living world and threw her mind into a deep blackness that contained only the ever-stormy nightmares of the Undertow. In the horrible, chaotic maelstrom of bizarre sensations and feelings never meant for mortal eyes, she forced her will, shaped in her head the image of a twisted, many-eyed octopus. As she concentrated on the vision, two of the fish's eyes were torn out of its head in a slimly plop. They stared at the chaos around them and floated in the air, untouched by the raging water and wind.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Your eyes shall be mine", she said in a dry whisper, reached out for the eyes and closed her fist around them. As she felt the large, slimy things against her skin, the storm in her mind quieted and she once again stood on the shore.[PARAGRAPH:2]"And my eyes they will be", she finished, now seeing with two pairs of eyes as she opened her fists to reveal the gifts of her gods. She said nothing more as she lowered her hands and willed the eyes to rise up in the air, go out and spy upon the enemies of the Undertow.

[TAB]"My lady... the results of your experiment. Nearly all of them... twisted beyond comprehension..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Those who weren't cut out for this shouldn't have volunteered," the voice of the priestess was as harsh and merciless as the young man's was quivering. "The ones who perish here wouldn't have survived combat anyway."[PARAGRAPH:1]The men and the women who'd volunteered lay prone on the open field, all covered by monstrous deformities. One seemed to have had all the blood sucked out of him, another man's testicles had grown so huge they had crushed his toes under their weight. The priestess was walking among them, inspecting each before moving on. Clearly, it seemed, one of the ones who wasn't cut out for it was the aide she'd been assigned.[PARAGRAPH:1]"But my lady," he tried one more time, flinching away his gaze from the man whose bowels had exploded rather violently out of his stomach, "There wasn't anything wrong with these troops, that's why you chose them... they would have made excellent soldiers had not..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"And you would make an excellent Drown if you did not shut up," the priestess replied coldly, finally quieting the aide. She stopped in front of one of her test subjects, pausing to take a closer look. The elven woman had been pretty once, but no stretch of the imagination would let you use that word of her anymore. Any fat she might have had was muscle now, and all the muscle she had was grown large enough to stretch and tear away the skin that had once covered it. Her eyes were bulging out of her head, the expanding tissue having forced them out of their sockets-but despite everything, she eyed the priestess with an air of wary satisfaction.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I think this... is exactly what we need," for the first time today, a smile slowly appeared on the priestess's lips. Her eyes glowing, she turned to the aide, joyous laughter in her voice. "I knew the Undertow would not forsake us! They have gifted some of us inhuman strength, enough to take down all of our foes. Find the others who look like this, they're the ones we want."[PARAGRAPH:1]"And... the others?" the man slowly asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]"The others? Oh," the priestess shrugged, having entirely forgotten about the failures already, "I don't think they can be made into Drown anymore, can they? It really doesn't matter, do what you want with them." She turned away from the aide, smiling and looking at the elven woman with love and adoration in her eyes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"You are so pretty that way, my dear. I'm so glad you made it."

[TAB]The Kraken's swimming was slow, leisurely. Thoughts took a while to cross from one edge of its immense brain to the other, the movements of its tentacles almost independent of its mind. Somewhere, far away on the surface, it could faintly sense a distant call which it couldn't resist. But it was not yet in any rush, instinctively knowing that the caller would need time to prepare.[PARAGRAPH:1]In a lazy motion, one of its tentacles made a slow wave around it, dozens of the small fish surrounding it getting caught in the suction cups. It brought the tentacle back to one of its mouths, dined on its snack. A huge swarm of fish followed it wherever it went-countless of them would end up as its meal, but even more would get to dine on its bigger catches. The swarm stretched back for tens of miles, twice as far as the Kraken itself.[PARAGRAPH:1]Gradually it started getting closer to the surface, could feel the call growing more and more demanding. The fish dispersed in fright and then reassembled as the Kraken began swimming faster, faster than it usually ever did. The alien presence was now a burning sun buried in its brain, no longer willing to tolerate any delay. For all of its size, dwarfing small islands, the Kraken was only a servant for the true lords of the sea.[PARAGRAPH:1]When the chosen of the Undertow called, it would obey and serve with all its might.

The Peliguard is a massive temple that is continuously being constructed by a race of powerful golems. They pay little attention to any of the petitioners, angels or even Nantosuelta herself unless anyone attempts to stop their work or damage the temple. In which case they react violently.[PARAGRAPH]The temple itself is an academy and arena in one. This is the place where angelic champions are trained and prepared for war. Most of this time is devoted to combat, but magic, siegecraft, armorsmithing, weaponsmithing, military strategy, history and mental, physical and spiritual endurance are also trained along with a wide variety of other subjects. Anything that helps prepare them to battle the forces of hell.[PARAGRAPH]This is one of the few vaults where angels of other dominions travel freely. Angels of the other good and neutral gods can often be found here training, or teaching.[PARAGRAPH]There are various, elaborate training programs. But the most intense is known as the Suffering. The Suffering is an assault on the body, mind and spirit of those going through it. Nantosuelta herself watches over the trial. And those that fail often do so by falling and becoming demons. If so Nantosuelta destroys them. Those that survive become paragons of faith. It has been said that no one that survives the Suffering will ever fall. And so far, that has been true. To these few are given the most sensitive of tasks, to bear an artifact that cannot be lost, to travel into the hells or to serve one that cannot be betrayed.
